sources.title: AESC Global Guide to Choosing an Executive Search Firm
EURES: Boost your career with a strong online presence

definitions.label: Targeted cold application
definitions.purpose: Submit directly to a known opportunity without relying on a prior relationship.

actions: Evaluate configured hard gates.
Select one positioning thesis when tailoring requires it.
Record pass, mitigate, or stop with evidence.
Tailor the proposition and directly relevant evidence.
Select the exact artifacts intended for transmission.
Submit through the verified channel.
Record submission only after confirmation.
Record dated acknowledgement, response, progress, or rejection events.
Evaluate only mature confirmed submissions.

guardrails: Do not infer submission, response, or rejection.
Do not treat mass application as targeted cold application.

definitions.label: Warm introduction
definitions.purpose: Reach a relevant person through an existing trusted relationship.

actions: Confirm the connector, recipient, relevance, and objective.
Prepare a concise context-rich introduction request without implying sponsorship.
Send through the confirmed connector or channel.
Record only confirmed outreach.
Record reply, introduction, conversation, or explicit decline.

guardrails: Do not claim a referral or sponsorship that was not explicitly offered.

definitions.label: Hiring-leader outreach
definitions.purpose: Seek substantive calibration with the leader responsible for a mandate.

actions: Verify the leader's relationship to the mandate and the evidence behind the hypothesis.
Frame one mandate hypothesis, one relevant proof, and one useful question.
Send through the selected channel and preserve exact content when available.
Record substantive response, calibration conversation, or explicit decline.

guardrails: Do not bypass required recruiting processes or imply decision authority.

definitions.label: Executive-search market mapping
definitions.purpose: Build durable calibration relationships with relevant executive-search consultants before or around mandates.

actions: Identify relevant functions, sectors, geographies, firms, and consultants.
Prepare a stable executive brief and specific calibration questions.
Request a substantive market-calibration conversation.
Record conversations, feedback, future mapping, or mandate progress.

guardrails: Do not infer that a consultant represents a mandate or intends to submit the candidate.

definitions.label: Target-company campaign
definitions.purpose: Develop a focused relationship with selected organizations independent of a single advertised opportunity.

actions: Validate the company, business problem, leadership context, and plausible contribution.
Identify relevant leaders, connectors, recruiters, and public signals.
Start with a useful hypothesis or conversation rather than an invented opportunity.
Record conversations, referrals, invitations, or explicit non-fit.

guardrails: Do not fabricate a role, opening, relationship, or company need.

definitions.label: Internal mobility
definitions.purpose: Explore and pursue mandates within the current organization through appropriate internal channels.

actions: Verify internal policy, role facts, timing, and confidentiality boundaries.
Seek evidence-based conversations with relevant sponsors, peers, or talent partners.
Use the required formal internal process when pursuing a known role.
Record confirmed sponsorship, screening, progression, or closure.

guardrails: Do not infer sponsorship, confidentiality, or manager approval.

definitions.label: Authority building
definitions.purpose: Build credible visibility through useful public expertise and evidence.

actions: Choose a coherent expertise thesis and intended audience.
Create useful, evidence-bounded work in an appropriate format.
Publish only after explicit review and through an authorized channel.
Record substantive conversations, invitations, or recruiter contact without inferring causality.

guardrails: Publication is an external action requiring explicit authorization.
Do not publish private or employer-confidential evidence.

definitions.label: Community and event networking
definitions.purpose: Build relevant professional relationships through communities, conferences, and focused events.

actions: Choose communities or events aligned to the target mandate and geography.
Identify useful questions, peers, and contribution opportunities.
Participate substantively and follow up with explicit context.
Record continued conversations, introductions, and opportunities.

guardrails: Do not represent attendance, conversation, or consent that was not confirmed.
